bottlenecks: SensorPlacement._greedy (default algorithm) is O(S*T) per iteration — 10k sensors x 100k targets = 1B distance checks per pass; _greedy_indexed exists but is not the default
DeviceRegistry stores all devices in a single in-memory dict with no sharding — 1000+ devices cause O(N) scans for list_devices and get_offline_devices
TimescaleDBStorage.query does full table scan + sort on every query — no index hints, O(N log N) per read
KafkaStream.consume uses blocking queue.get per message with no batch polling overhead control
MQTTClient.publish iterates all subscribers linearly — O(S) per message with no topic trie index
DeviceAuth.validate_api_key uses SHA-256 without salt — vulnerable to rainbow table attacks on leaked hashes
DataValidator.validate is fail-fast per record with no batch validation API
AnomalyDetector recomputes mean/stddev from scratch on every update() — O(W) per reading instead of O(1) incremental
LoRaWANSimulator.send_uplink simulates SNR as a fixed value (10.0 or 5.0) — no real path-loss or fading model
ConsistentHashRing._build_ring is O(V*N) on every add_node/remove_node — rebuilds entire ring instead of incremental update
missing_algorithms: SensorPlacement: no optimal/exact solver (ILP, branch-and-bound) — only greedy Set Cover with no approximation ratio guarantee
SensorPlacement: no weighted set cover (sensor cost/energy/reliability)
SensorPlacement: no k-coverage / redundancy modeling for fault tolerance
SensorPlacement: no multi-objective optimization (Pareto frontier for coverage vs cost vs energy)
SensorPlacement: no parallel or distributed greedy for large-scale deployment
SensorPlacement: no incremental/dynamic reconfiguration when targets or sensors change
DeviceRegistry: no bulk operations (bulk_register, bulk_update_health, bulk_provision)
DeviceRegistry: no device grouping / tagging beyond simple list filter
DeviceRegistry: no consistent hashing / shard assignment for horizontal scaling
DeviceRegistry: no pagination for list_devices
DeviceRegistry: no device decommissioning workflow (data archival, cert revocation, dependent notification)
DeviceRegistry: no device capability discovery
AnomalyDetector: only z-score — no IQR, isolation forest, or EWMA-based detection
AnomalyDetector: no seasonality-aware detection (agriculture has strong diurnal/seasonal cycles)
AnomalyDetector: no incremental mean/stddev update (Welford's algorithm) — current is O(W) per reading
DataValidator: no data gap detection or interpolation (linear/spline/Kalman)
DataValidator: no calibration drift detection
DataValidator: no batch validation API for efficient bulk processing
DataValidator: no custom validator functions (regex, checksum, geographic bounds)
DataValidator: no nested object validation (recursive schema for nested dicts/lists)
DataValidator: no validation error severity levels (critical/warning/info)
DataValidator: no schema versioning/migration
No edge computing scheduler (task offloading, latency-aware placement, energy-aware scheduling)
No digital twin sync engine (bidirectional state reconciliation with conflict resolution)
No data lineage tracking (source, transformations, processing history)
No data versioning or rollback
No multi-tenancy support (tenant isolation, tenant-aware queries)
No data encryption at rest
MQTTClient: no QoS 1/2 support (only QoS 0 fire-and-forget)
MQTTClient: no retained messages (last-known-value for new subscribers)
MQTTClient: no Last Will and Testament (LWT) for graceful disconnect detection
MQTTClient: no TLS/SSL support (plaintext credentials and data)
MQTTClient: no authentication (username/password, token, mutual TLS)
KafkaStream: no schema registry integration (Avro/Protobuf/JSON Schema)
KafkaStream: no exactly-once semantics (idempotent producers, transactional consumers)
KafkaStream: no stream processing (windowing, joins, aggregations, CEP)
NGSILDBroker: no temporal API support (GET /temporal/entities)
NGSILDBroker: no geo API support (near, within, intersects)
NGSILDBroker: no subscription update (PATCH /subscriptions/{id})
NGSILDBroker: no @context resolution (JSON-LD compaction/expansion)
NGSILDBroker: no pagination (offset/cursor) for list_entities
NGSILDBroker: no batch operations (bulk create/update/delete)
